citations.description: Tests only capability derivation (caps.supports_temperature), not runner model_settings behavior
Runner-level temperature tests do not cover the supports_temperature=False path
Runner implementation that omits temperature when supports_temperature is False — untested at runner level

findings.criterion: a test asserts `temperature` is omitted for a model whose `supports_temperature` capability is False, and still sent for one where it is True (Decision C) — the contrast case
findings.detail: The tests in `tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py` (e.g. `test_supports_temperature_is_withdrawn_only_for_the_measured_model`) only verify the CAPABILITY DERIVATION — that `caps.supports_temperature` is False for the measured model and True for the OK model. No test exercises the RUNNER BEHAVIOR: that `temperature` is actually absent from `model_settings` when `supports_temperature` is False, and present when True. The runner logic at `runner.py:399-408` implements this, but `test_llm_temperature.py` (the runner-level temperature test file) contains no test for the `supports_temperature=False` path, and no other test file exercises this contrast case at the runner level.

citations.description: Test asserts model id and parameter but not both remedies
Implementation includes both remedies in the message, but the test does not assert them
Contrast case asserts translate_sampling_parameter_rejection returns None, not that the runner produces LLMUnavailableError

findings.criterion: a test asserts a provider error matching the MEASURED shape (400 / ValidationException + a sampling parameter name + a rejection word) becomes an `LLMConfigError` naming the model id, the parameter, and both remedies — and a CONTRAST case asserts an unrelated 400 still becomes `LLMUnavailableError`
findings.detail: The test `test_sampling_parameter_rejection_becomes_an_actionable_config_error` asserts the model id and parameter are in the error message, but does NOT assert that both remedies are present (the AC explicitly requires 'naming the model id, the parameter, and both remedies'). The implementation at `failure.py:403-410` does include both remedies, but the test does not verify them. Additionally, the contrast case `test_unrelated_provider_failures_are_not_swallowed_by_the_translation` asserts `translate_sampling_parameter_rejection` returns `None` for unrelated failures, but does not assert the runner produces `LLMUnavailableError` — the AC says 'a CONTRAST case asserts an unrelated 400 still becomes `LLMUnavailableError`'.
